title: Lockstep run on the right block
statement: Let $k,l$ be nonnegative integers, let $S,S'$ be state sets, and let $x$ be a finite Boolean input. Let $M$ have $l$ work tapes and state set $S$, and let $M'$ have $k+l$ work tapes and state set $S'$. Suppose $f:S\to S'$ satisfies the following transition rule: for every state $q\in S$, input symbol (possibly blank) $a$, and tuple $w$ of symbols on the $k+l$ work tapes, the transition of $M'$ at state $f(q)$ on $a,w$ is the right-block extension along $f$ of the transition of $M$ at $q$ on $a$ and the symbols of $w$ on the last $l$ tapes. Then, from any configuration $c$ of $M$ and any contents and head positions for the first $k$ tapes, the run of $M'$ for $t$ steps from the configuration that places $c$ on the last $l$ tapes and those data on the first $k$ tapes equals the configuration obtained by placing the run of $M$ for $t$ steps from $c$ on the last $l$ tapes and preserving the first $k$ tapes' data.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ has $l$ work tapes over Bool and state set $S$
$M'$ has $k+l$ work tapes over Bool and state set $S'$

replaced:
Let $M$ be a machine with $l$ work tapes and $M'$ a machine with $k + l$ work
tapes, both over the Boolean alphabet, and let $f$ be a map from the states
of $M$ to the states of $M'$ such that on every renamed state, for all
scanned symbols, the transition of $M'$ is the right-block extension along
$f$ of the corresponding transition of $M$ read off the last $l$ tapes.  Then
for every configuration $c$ of $M$ on input $x$, all inactive contents and
head positions for the first $k$ tapes, and every number of steps $t$,
running $M'$ for $t$ steps from the right-block embedding of $c$ equals the
right-block embedding of the run of $M$ for $t$ steps from $c$, with the
inactive left-block data preserved throughout.
